name: Ansible Content Management
description: Develop, certify, version, and distribute ansible content collections through automation hub, centralized content catalog, and development workspaces with GitOps-driven platform configuration.

narratives.name: From Ad Hoc Playbooks to Governed Content Distribution
narratives.description: The journey from unmanaged ansible scripts to a governed, catalog-driven content development and distribution pipeline.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations begin content management by recognizing the need to move beyond ad hoc playbook sharing and establish a centralized approach to ansible content development, versioning, and distribution through automation hub.

Content architecture decisions include collection namespace taxonomy, repository structure for GitOps configuration, workspace template specifications, and certification pipeline design aligning content governance with organizational security and quality standards.

Content developers use browser-based development workspaces with pre-configured tooling to create structured collections, while platform engineers implement GitOps configuration repositories using the infra.controller_configuration collection to manage platform state declaratively through the platform gateway.

Automated testing validates collection functionality using molecule, ansible-test, and ansible-lint within development workspaces, while CI/CD pipelines enforce quality gates including security scanning, digital signature verification, and peer review before content reaches production.

Certified collections are published to private automation hub with digital signatures, the centralized content catalog auto-discovers content from Git repositories and hub, and GitOps pipelines apply controller configuration changes through platform gateway on git push events.

Content lifecycle operations include monitoring collection usage analytics, managing semantic versioning and deprecation, automated drift detection for controller configuration, and continuous improvement of workspace templates and certification pipelines.

narratives.name: Building a Governed Content Supply Chain for Ansible Automation
narratives.description: How organizations progress from ad hoc playbook sharing to a certified, catalog-driven content distribution model.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations begin with individual developers creating standalone playbooks and sharing them informally. Collections are installed directly from Ansible Galaxy without version pinning or security review, leading to inconsistent automation behavior across environments and teams.

A private automation hub centralizes content distribution, collection namespaces enforce organizational taxonomy, and basic certification gates ensure quality. Development workspaces standardize the authoring environment so all content developers operate with consistent tooling versions and configurations.

A mature content supply chain features automated CI/CD pipelines that build, test, sign, and publish collections on merge. The centralized content catalog auto-discovers content from multiple sources, RBAC controls govern content visibility, and analytics track adoption and value delivery across the organization.

narratives.name: Maturing the Ansible Content Supply Chain
narratives.description: The organizational journey from ungoverned content consumption to automated, catalog-driven content distribution.

narrativeContexts.context: Teams install collections directly from Ansible Galaxy without version governance, leading to dependency conflicts and inconsistent automation behavior. Playbooks reference specific module versions that may differ across environments, creating hard-to-diagnose failures.

A private automation hub provides a single source of truth for approved content. Collection upload requires approver authorization, Red Hat Certified Content is synchronized from the cloud hub, and execution environments resolve dependencies from the private hub rather than external sources.

Automated certification pipelines enforce quality gates including security scanning, linting, and digital signature verification before any collection reaches production. The centralized content catalog auto-discovers content from Git repositories and private hub, providing unified visibility with RBAC-controlled access across the organization.

narratives.name: From Manual Configuration to GitOps-Driven Platform Management
narratives.description: The journey from ad hoc platform administration to fully declarative, version-controlled platform configuration.

narrativeContexts.context: Platform administrators create projects, inventories, and job templates manually through the controller web UI. Configuration changes lack audit trails, environment consistency depends on manual replication, and there is no systematic approach to managing platform state.

Projects are sourced from Git repositories with branch-based promotion workflows separating development from production. Pull request reviews provide change validation, tag-based releases freeze versions for critical deployments, and SCM integration ensures teams always execute the latest approved automation content.

Full GitOps management treats the entire controller configuration as code using the infra.controller_configuration collection. CI/CD pipelines apply configuration changes through the platform gateway on every commit, scheduled drift detection identifies unauthorized changes, and automated reconciliation maintains desired state.

narratives.name: Ansible Collection Development from Skeleton to Certified Distribution
narratives.description: How ansible content collections mature from standalone playbooks to certified, governed distribution artifacts.

narrativeContexts.context: The collection development process begins with identifying a recurring automation pattern that warrants codification and evaluating existing community or certified content for reuse before initiating new development.

Collection architecture follows the ansible-galaxy init skeleton, with galaxy.yml defining namespace taxonomy, semantic version, and dependency declarations that enable deterministic dependency resolution across consuming execution environments.
Content developers author modules, plugins, and roles within standardized development workspaces, implementing idempotent automation patterns and documenting variable interfaces for consuming teams.
Automated test suites use molecule for integration testing, ansible-test for sanity checks, and ansible-lint for style enforcement, ensuring collection quality before publication.

Certified collections are published to private automation hub with digital signatures, the centralized content catalog auto-discovers them, and RBAC controls govern visibility to appropriate consuming teams.

Collection maintainers track usage analytics, manage semantic versioning for backward compatibility, address issues through Git-based workflows, and document deprecation timelines when successor content is available.

narratives.name: Declarative Platform Management Through Version-Controlled Configuration
narratives.description: How controller configuration evolves from manual web UI administration to automated, drift-detected GitOps management.

narrativeContexts.context: Administrators create controller resources manually through the web UI, resulting in undocumented configuration changes and environment drift that is discovered only when deployments fail.

Configuration scripts using the platform gateway API introduce version control and repeatability, though idempotency challenges require careful error handling and scripts may not gracefully manage pre-existing resources.

Full declarative GitOps using the infra.controller_configuration collection treats the entire controller state as code, with CI/CD-driven application, automated drift detection, compliance validation, and approval workflows providing complete configuration governance.

narratives.description: How teams identify which infrastructure patterns warrant codification as reusable ansible content collections.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations accumulate ad hoc playbooks addressing recurring infrastructure patterns, but without systematic evaluation these remain one-off scripts rather than reusable, governed content collections that could benefit multiple teams.

Evaluate recurring infrastructure automation patterns to determine which warrant formal codification as collections, assess existing community and Red Hat Certified Content for reuse, and document build-vs-reuse decisions with rationale.

Survey consuming teams to identify repeated automation patterns, evaluate Ansible Galaxy and Red Hat Certified Content catalogs for existing coverage, document collection namespace planning following organizational taxonomy, and assess development workspace requirements.

A prioritized backlog of content development initiatives exists, each with documented rationale for build versus reuse, namespace taxonomy alignment, and development resource requirements, enabling systematic content ecosystem growth.

activities.name: Develop Ansible Content Collection
activities.description: Create, test, and publish ansible content collections as versioned distributable automation units.

narratives.name: Authoring Reusable Ansible Collections from Initialization to Publication
narratives.description: The development workflow for creating ansible content collections using development workspaces, testing tools, and automation hub publication.

narrativeContexts.context: Collection development begins with identifying a recurring automation pattern that warrants codification, evaluating existing community or Red Hat Certified Content for reuse, and planning the collection namespace and module architecture within the organizational taxonomy.

Initialize the collection structure using ansible-creator or ansible-galaxy collection init, defining the galaxy.yml metadata with namespace, version, dependencies, and supported platforms, then organizing modules, plugins, roles, and playbooks into the standardized directory layout.

Author Python modules implementing argument_spec definitions with parameter types and validation, create roles with idempotent task logic and Jinja2 templates, and develop playbooks demonstrating collection usage patterns within the pre-configured development workspace environment.

Execute automated validation using ansible-test sanity for static analysis, ansible-lint for playbook quality enforcement, molecule for integration testing across target platforms, and tox-ansible for cross-version compatibility, all within the development workspace.

Build the collection artifact using ansible-galaxy collection build, publish to private automation hub with authentication tokens, apply GPG digital signatures for integrity verification, and document the release with semantic versioning and changelog.

Monitor collection usage through hub analytics, manage backward-compatible version updates following semantic versioning, address reported issues through Git-based workflows, and deprecate superseded collections with documented migration guidance.

activities.name: Provision Content Development Workspaces
activities.description: Deploy and manage browser-based development workspace environments with pre-configured ansible tooling.

narratives.name: Standardizing Content Development Through Managed Workspaces
narratives.description: How platform teams provision and govern browser-based development environments to ensure consistent content creation.

narrativeContexts.context: Content developers install ansible tools locally with varying versions and configurations, leading to inconsistent automation behavior, environment-specific failures, and time-consuming setup for new team members.
Provide browser-based pre-configured development environments with standardized tooling versions and organizational coding standards enforced through workspace templates.

Create workspace templates specifying approved tool versions, linting configurations, and Git integration. Deploy workspaces centrally with platform administrator control over security policies, approved VS Code extensions, network access controls, and resource limits.

All content developers operate in consistent, governed environments where tool versions match production requirements, organizational coding standards are enforced automatically, and new team members become productive within hours rather than days.

activities.name: Certify Ansible Content
activities.description: Execute content quality gates including security scanning, linting validation, and digital signature application.

narratives.name: Enforcing Content Quality Through Automated Certification Pipelines
narratives.description: How organizations implement automated quality gates ensuring only certified, signed content reaches production automation workflows.

narrativeContexts.context: Without formal certification, ansible collections of varying quality and security posture enter the organizational content ecosystem, creating risk of vulnerable dependencies, inconsistent automation behavior, and difficulty tracing content provenance.

Establish an automated certification pipeline that enforces quality standards, validates security posture, verifies content integrity through digital signatures, and routes approvals to domain experts before publication.

Configure automation hub to require certification for published collections, integrate security scanning into CI/CD pipelines, implement GPG-based digital signing for content integrity verification, and establish approval workflows routing collections to designated domain expert reviewers.

All organizational content meets documented quality and security standards before reaching consumers, content provenance is verifiable through digital signatures, deprecated or vulnerable collections are automatically flagged, and certification status is visible in the automation hub UI.

activities.name: Configure Content Catalog Discovery
activities.description: Configure centralized content catalog to auto-discover collections from Git repositories and private hub sources.

narratives.name: Unified Content Visibility Through Centralized Catalog Auto-Discovery
narratives.description: How the centralized content catalog provides unified visibility across all organizational content sources.

narrativeContexts.context: Ansible content is distributed across multiple private hub instances, Git repositories, and community sources, making it difficult for consumers to discover available automation, assess quality, and select the most appropriate collection.

Deploy and configure the AAP 2.7 centralized content catalog to auto-discover collections from all organizational content sources, providing unified visibility with RBAC-controlled access governing what content different teams can discover and consume.

Configure the centralized content catalog with Git repository connections and private hub integration, establish RBAC visibility controls per team and organization, validate auto-discovery of existing collections, and set up content usage analytics to track adoption metrics.

All organizational content is discoverable through a single catalog interface, RBAC controls ensure teams see only content they are authorized to consume, content usage analytics inform investment decisions, and the catalog automatically reflects new collections as they are published.

activities.name: Establish Content SCM Workflows
activities.description: Configure automation controller projects with Git repository source control and branch-based promotion workflows.

narratives.name: Progressive SCM Integration for Ansible Content Projects
narratives.description: How to migrate from manually managed playbooks to branch-based development workflows with environment promotion.

narrativeContexts.context: Configure automation controller projects with Git repository URLs and branch specifications, set up SCM credentials for private repository access, and enable project sync to fetch playbooks from version control rather than direct filesystem management.

Establish separate controller projects for development, staging, and production branches, implement update-on-launch for templates ensuring latest content, and configure project sync failure alerts that provide actionable error messages to content developers.

Implement pull request workflows requiring peer review before merging to production branches, use tag-based releases to freeze playbook versions for critical deployments, and enforce branch protection rules preventing direct commits to production branches.

activities.name: Implement GitOps Platform Configuration
activities.description: Manage automation controller configuration as code using version-controlled declarative YAML through platform gateway.

narratives.name: Declarative Controller Management with infra.controller_configuration
narratives.description: How to implement GitOps-driven configuration management for the automation controller using version-controlled YAML.

narrativeContexts.context: Determine the repository structure for controller configuration, choosing between single-file and modular approaches, and defining the scope separation between global platform settings and organization-specific resources.

Install the infra.controller_configuration and awx.awx collections, create the configure_controller.yml playbook importing roles for each resource type in dependency order, and configure controller connection variables pointing to the platform gateway endpoint.

Define resources in YAML following the controller_configuration schema: projects with SCM URLs and branch specifications, inventories with organization assignments, job templates with project/inventory/credential associations, and workflow job templates with node topology definitions.

Execute configuration playbooks in dry-run mode to validate syntax and permissions before applying to the production controller, and set up development controllers where configuration changes are auto-applied for rapid feedback.

Configure CI/CD pipeline integration to apply configuration on git push events through the platform gateway with service account authentication, implementing approval gates for production changes while enabling auto-apply for development environments.

Implement scheduled drift detection comparing desired state in Git against actual state queried through the platform gateway API, configure alerting for unauthorized manual changes, and establish automated reconciliation to revert configuration drift.

activities.name: Monitor Content Lifecycle Operations
activities.description: Track content usage analytics, manage collection versioning, and execute content deprecation and retirement.

narratives.name: Continuous Improvement of the Organizational Content Ecosystem
narratives.description: How content lifecycle operations use analytics and feedback to continuously improve the organizational content ecosystem.

narrativeContexts.context: Define content lifecycle metrics including collection download counts, consuming team adoption rates, issue resolution times, and version currency across the organization, establishing baselines and improvement targets.

Implement collection usage tracking through automation hub analytics, establish semantic versioning policies for backward compatibility, create deprecation procedures with consumer notification timelines, and execute content retirement workflows.

Review content usage analytics to identify under-adopted collections needing promotion, over-extended collections needing refactoring, and deprecated collections still in use by consuming teams, comparing actual metrics against established targets.

Act on findings by promoting high-value collections, deprecating low-adoption content with documented migration paths, refactoring complex collections into focused units, and updating content development standards based on quality patterns observed.

activities.name: Retire Automation Content
activities.description: Deprecate, migrate consumers, and archive superseded ansible content collections.

narratives.name: Governed Content Retirement Preventing Orphaned Automation Dependencies
narratives.description: How to systematically retire ansible content collections while ensuring consuming teams migrate to successors.

narrativeContexts.context: Collections inevitably reach end-of-life due to successor content availability, technology deprecation, or organizational changes, but ungoverned retirement creates orphaned automation dependencies that fail silently in production.

Implement a governed content retirement process that identifies successor collections, communicates deprecation timelines to consuming teams, provides migration guidance, and ensures all consumers migrate before final archive.

Publish deprecation notices in automation hub and centralized content catalog, create consumer migration guides with version compatibility matrices, set automated alerts to teams still consuming deprecated collections, and archive retired collections with read-only access for audit purposes.

Content retirement follows a predictable, governed process where no collection is removed without successor validation, consumer migration is tracked to completion, and audit trails maintain the complete provenance of retired content.
